site_name: Lake Mariner Data Campus, bitcoin mining
serving_utility: NYSEG transmission interconnection (Kintigh 345 kV); energy from the NYISO Zone A market plus a 90 MW NYPA allocation
load_basis: Built bitcoin mining capacity operated as of 2025-12-31, per TeraWulf FY2025 10-K. Capacity, not average draw: the same 10-K reports 1,344,760 MWh used by its bitcoin mining facilities in 2025, about 153 MW on average.
notes: NEW ROW, not a duplicate: the two inventory rows at this campus (epoch:Core42 Lake Mariner, epoch:Anthropic Lake Mariner) are the HPC buildings; the 245 MW mining load on the same campus is not in the inventory. 10-K: campus is in Barker on about 157 leased acres in Niagara County, at the former Somerset coal plant; mining began March 2022. The 10-K gives no street address; coordinates are the Census-geocoder point for 7725 Lake Rd, Barker (an address I did not find in a fetched source) and are identical to the inventory's epoch coordinates. Utility: the 10-K says power is sourced from the NYISO Zone A grid with 90 MW under a ten-year NYPA high-load-factor agreement; it does not name a delivery utility or say whether purchases are direct or through a supplier, so 'wholesale_direct' is my reading and I am uncertain about it. NYSEG and the Kintigh 345 kV point of interconnection come from a third-party copy of a NYISO queue entry for a later 250 MW TeraWulf load project (https://www.infrasure.ai/project/nyiso-1732-wulf-compute-data-center-ii), not from a NYSEG or PSC document. The 2025 MWh figure is labeled in the 10-K as Lake Mariner plus any net Nautilus (Pennsylvania) share; I believe the Nautilus interest was sold in 2024 but did not verify that here. 2024 comparable: 1,601,061 MWh including the Nautilus share.

site_name: Lake Mariner Data Campus, HPC hosting (Core42 buildings)
serving_utility: NYSEG transmission interconnection (Kintigh 345 kV); energy from the NYISO Zone A market plus a 90 MW NYPA allocation
load_basis: Critical IT MW of HPC capacity energized as of 2025-12-31, per TeraWulf FY2025 10-K (Core42 leases; 60 MW critical IT committed to Core42 in total).
notes: HPC leasing began July 2025. Only 18 critical IT MW was energized at year-end 2025, against 58 MW in the inventory for 2025. Contracted HPC at the campus is 438 MW critical IT (60 MW Core42 plus 378 MW Fluidstack, Fluidstack delivery expected to start in 2026). Planned figure is campus gross capacity including mining: about 500 MW near term, about 750 MW potential subject to further NYISO approval. Flag on epoch:Anthropic Lake Mariner (2026, 210 MW): the 10-K names Fluidstack, not Anthropic, as the 378 MW Lake Mariner tenant, and TeraWulf's 2026 press release titles place its Anthropic lease at the Justified Data Campus in Kentucky (https://investors.terawulf.com/news-events/press-releases). I could not confirm an Anthropic tenancy at Lake Mariner. Utility caveats are the same as on the mining row.

operator: Coinmint (North Country Colocation Services / North Country Data Center Corp.; NYDIG strategic stake since 2024)
serving_utility: No retail utility named; operator says it buys directly from NYISO, not through Massena Electric Department or NYPA
load_basis: Operating load reported in a trade article dated 2024-11-21 ('currently utilizing 166 MW of its approved 435 MW'). This is a late-2024 figure, not a 2025 measurement: hosting customers were due to vacate about 66% of that capacity around year-end 2024, with NYDIG expected to backfill. No 2025 figure found.
notes: NEW ROW. Possibly the second-largest data center load in the state, and the 2025 number is the weakest in this file; treat 166 MW as an upper-range placeholder. Earlier operator statements: 145 MW in Q1 2022 and 80 to 100 MW during 2021 (North Country Now, 2022-05-21). Operations began June 2018 on a 10-year Alcoa lease. Conflict on power supply: the operator's 2022 statement says power comes straight from NYISO, while The Block (2026-04-18, https://www.theblock.co/amp/post/397983/alcoa-nears-deal-to-sell-dormant-new-york-smelter-site-to-bitcoin-miner-nydig-bloomberg) says the Massena East site draws NYPA hydropower. Coordinates are the centroid of the OpenStreetMap polygon named 'Alcoa - St-Lawrence - Massena, Smelter' east of the village near Akwesasne, which I take to be the Alcoa East plant; no street address was found in a fetched source, so treat the point as approximate.

site_name: Greenidge Generation power plant and datacenter
operator: Greenidge Generation Holdings (EDGAR now lists the registrant as Vulcan Infrastructure & Power Inc.)
serving_utility: None: self-supplied behind the meter from Greenidge's own gas plant (about 106 MW nameplate), which also sells into NYISO
load_basis: FY2025 10-K: owned and customer-hosted miners at the New York facility 'had the capacity to consume approximately 60 MW' as of 2025-12-31. Capacity, not average draw; the company curtails mining to sell power to the grid.
notes: Behind the meter, so this load does not pass through a retail utility. NYISO approval covers 64 MW of behind-the-meter use. Pilot mining of about 1 MW began May 2019; the commercial datacenter launched January 2020; about 51 MW by year-end 2021 (FY2021 10-K). The 10-K places the plant in the Town of Torrey and names no street address; 'Dresden' and the coordinates come from the inventory's OpenStreetMap feature. The company says it is pursuing conversion of the site to AI/HPC use.

site_name: Hut 8 Alpha (former US Bitcoin Corp site), Buffalo Avenue
load_basis: Site capacity in Hut 8's FY2025 10-K table of assets under management as of 2025-12-31 (Alpha, Niagara Falls NY, NYISO grid, ASIC compute, 50 MW, 100% owned). Capacity, not average draw.
notes: Hut 8's filings name only 'NYISO grid'; no delivery utility or power contract was found, so the utility is left null. First-energized year not found in a fetched source (inventory has 2020; not verified). The Buffalo Avenue location and 50 MW size are also in a 2023-04-06 CoinDesk report carried by Yahoo Finance (https://uk.finance.yahoo.com/news/u-bitcoin-corp-expected-settle-151600836.html); a court halted the site in March 2023 over noise and a city settlement followed in April 2023. Per the 10-K, a third-party hosting contract at Alpha ended and the site is now used only for self-mining, with American Bitcoin miners on site. Coordinates are the inventory's OpenStreetMap feature.

site_name: Blockfusion Niagara Falls campus (North East Data LLC), Frontier Avenue
load_basis: Operator-level description: a 2026-07-01 trade article says Blockfusion 'currently operates a 50-megawatt facility in Niagara Falls', and blockfusion.com advertises '50MW of rack space'. Nameplate, not measured 2025 draw.
notes: One campus drawn in the inventory as eleven OpenStreetMap buildings named 'Blockfusion Niagra Falls' (osm:way/832656125, 832656868, 832658041, 1229749890 through 1229749896, 1442054199); treat them as a single site and do not count them separately. I could not tell what osm:way/832622369 (operator Blockfusion, about 5 km east, start 2019) is. Operating status in 2025 is uncertain in scale: the city issued a cease-and-desist in October 2022, and Blockfusion's December 2025 S-4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1910992/000118518525001952/blockfusions4110825.htm) says it continues to earn revenue hosting bitcoin miners for existing customers during its transition to AI hosting, without a MW figure in the portions I could read. The company describes the site as a converted decommissioned power plant drawing hydroelectric and nuclear power in NYISO Zone A; no utility is named. Planned: letter of intent for up to 300 MW critical IT, first 85 MW phase with deliveries from 2027; a CoreWeave lease was announced 2026-09-16.

site_name: Digi Power X (Digihost) North Tonawanda power plant and mining site
operator: Digi Power X Inc. (formerly Digihost Technology); plant subsidiary World Generation X, LLC
serving_utility: Self-supplied from the company's own 60 MW North Tonawanda gas plant (formerly Fortistar North Tonawanda)
notes: NEW ROW, load not established. Address 1070 Erie Ave (FY2025 10-K), geocoded with the Census geocoder. The company bought the plant on 2023-02-08. Sources disagree on how the site runs: Earthjustice (2024-11) says Digihost uses the plant to power mining on site and ramped it toward round-the-clock operation; the FY2025 10-K says the plant 'currently operates as a peaker plant' serving the grid and does not describe it as behind the meter. No operating mining MW for this site was found. A 2022-10-04 company report said that 'with the power plant running at 50 MW' its capacity would rise about 150% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1854368/000117184322006390/exh_992.htm); that is a plan, so load is left null. The 10-K lists '123 MW secured in North Tonawanda', which I recorded as the planned figure though it conflicts with the 60 MW plant size. Plant size is given as 55 MW by Earthjustice and 60 MW by the company. A November 2024 court ruling sent the PSC's approval of the sale back for review, and the city imposed a two-year moratorium on new mining and AI data centers in July 2024.

site_name: Digi Power X (Digihost) Buffalo mining facility, 1001 East Delavan Ave
operator: Digi Power X Inc. (formerly Digihost Technology)
load_basis: Power capacity 'secured' at the Buffalo site per the FY2025 10-K (the line reads '18.7 MW secured in Buffalo Alabama' under the Upstate New York heading, an apparent typo). Secured capacity, not operating load.
notes: NEW ROW. Address from the 10-K (over 60,000 sq ft on a 99-year lease). Coordinates are the OpenStreetMap industrial parcel addressed 1001 East Delavan Avenue (https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/1077210020); the Census geocoder did not match the address. The site came into the company through a reverse takeover that closed 2020-02-14; the year mining began there was not found. The 10-K describes it as grid-powered but names no utility. The 10-K also says the company's three sites have about 90 MW of available operating power in total (two in New York, one in Alabama).

serving_utility: NYPA hydropower allocations; delivery utility likely NYSEG, not confirmed
load_basis: Sum of NYPA low-cost hydropower allocations: 15 MW for the original data center plus 7.2 MW for the 2015 expansion and customer care center. Contracted hydropower, a likely lower bound; not metered load and not built IT capacity.
notes: Year correction: Phase I was built May 2009 to September 2010 (state senate release), so the inventory's 2023 start year is wrong. Load caution: the inventory carries 90.4 MW, which is about four times the NYPA allocations and may reflect backup-generator nameplate; I found no source for actual load or built IT capacity, so do not treat 22.2 MW as a measured replacement. A 2011 article adds 1 MW more hydropower for Phase 2 (https://datacenterknowledge.com/energy-power-supply/yahoo-gets-power-for-buffalo-expansion), which would make 23.2 MW. Part of the 7.2 MW serves the call center rather than servers. NYSEG appears in the sources only as the conduit for a DOE efficiency grant, so its role as delivery utility is an inference. Coordinates are the inventory's.

site_name: JPMorgan Chase Orangeburg data center campus, 140 Old Orangeburg Road
notes: No published MW found for the existing building or the expansion, so the inventory's 137.1 MW is unconfirmed. bi:779-0 (about 30 m away, same operator) is the same campus and should not be counted separately. Utility: News 12 (2026-04-23) reports Orange and Rockland Utilities saying it is reviewing the expansion's impact on the grid; that supports O&R as the serving utility but says nothing about the tariff. JPMorgan's first county IDA deal was in 2017; the opening year of the first building was not found (inventory has 2020). A second building on the campus is expected by 2028. Coordinates are the inventory's; the Census geocoder puts 140 Old Orangeburg Rd at 41.0443, -73.9740, about 0.9 km south.

site_name: DataBank Orangeburg campus (LGA3, LGA4), 2000 Corporate Dr
load_basis: Critical IT load DataBank lists for LGA3 (built capacity as marketed, not measured load). LGA4 adds 10 MW critical IT but its page is written in the future tense, so it is not counted for 2025.
notes: Matches the inventory's 20 MW. DataBank says the campus is fed from 'an existing utility-owned substation providing 30MW' (expandable to 45 MW, with room for a second 45 MW DataBank-owned substation) but does not name the utility; Orangeburg is in Orange and Rockland territory by map only, so the utility is left null. Opening date not stated on DataBank's pages (inventory has 2024). Planned figure is the 30 MW campus critical IT load DataBank lists; the LGA3 page separately mentions 40 MW of power when complete. Route Fifty (2026-04) reports CoreWeave leasing part of the DataBank facility. Coordinates are the Census-geocoder point for the published address.

Year correction only: Route Fifty's republication of a New York Focus story (2026-04) says 'Bloomberg opened a data center there in 2014', against 2025 in the inventory. No MW found; size relative to the 10 MW threshold is unknown. Coordinates are the inventory's.

load_basis: Operator page dated 2025-04-10: the data center 'currently delivers 4 MW of IT load, with plans for a 30 MW expansion'.
notes: Below the 10 MW threshold today; included because it sizes an unsized known facility. Planned figure is 4 MW existing plus the 30 MW expansion, which is my addition. Route Fifty (2026-04) reports Morgan Stanley and Natixis taking space here. Coordinates are the inventory's.

load_basis: Sabey's site page: '18 MW of aggregate power delivered to the campus'. Delivered power capacity, not measured load; the page is undated, so the as-of date is the 2026 fetch.
notes: NEW ROW; no inventory facility at this address. First phase powered up March 2013 with 5.4 MW 'from ConEd' (Commercial Property Executive, 2013-03-29); design goal 40 MW of critical capacity. Coordinates are the Census-geocoder point for 375 Pearl St.

load_basis: Hosted capacity one customer (Bit Digital) planned to keep at Coinmint's Plattsburgh site, per a trade article dated 2024-11-21. Not total site load, and a late-2024 figure.
notes: NEW ROW, thin. Only one sourced figure and no address, opening year or utility found in a fetched source; coordinates left null. County is the City of Plattsburgh's county. Drop this row if a located, dated record is required.
